title: One number, and what it cannot say (worked out on cardboard)
note: The authored thinking for one hall, in the first person, by the pass (Claude), for Palle's request of 2026-11-14 (see Russell_Paradox.json). 'at' is the floor's own frame in metres (x east, z south), 'yaw' in degrees. A sticker of kind 'quote' stands word for word in the hall text; every other kind is mine and may be wrong - the plates say where I am unsure.

hero.why: The console is what the hall text is about: four rails, one returned number, and KEEP. The formula hangs behind it, as the text says.
hero.staging: The console stood at the far north edge with its back to the arrival, and the formula hung on the south edge behind the arriving visitor; the pass restaged the floor (53bb39961). The console is straight ahead of the arrival, turned to face it, the formula behind and above it, the two rails at either hand, the three spheres at the visitor's left; behind the formula the painted floor.

plates.title: 1  THE FORMULA RETURNS A NUMBER
front: One floor up the formula waited to be questioned. Here it answers: I move a rail and a number changes.
That is a different kind of thing. A sentence I could doubt; a readout I tend to believe.
What it computes: F minus lambda times E, plus phi times 0.3. Four rails from nought to one. That is all.
The 0.3 is fixed. Nobody measured it. The hall says so, which I did not expect of a hall with a console in it.
So: an arithmetic I can inspect. Not a measurement of anything living.
back: F here is a rail named after Friston's quantity. it computes none of it. I looked at the console's code: the whole calculation is one line.

plates.title: 2  ONE NUMBER, A WHOLE LINE OF PLACES
front: The hall asks: can two different arrangements give the same number? On the console I found a pair after some fiddling.
On the floor behind the formula I am two of the rails. East is F, north is E. I stood still at F 0.70, E 0.50 and it kept the place: 0.45.
Then a red line: every place with 0.45. Not a pair. A whole line of them, 6.7 metres long.
I walked it. The big number did not move. The shape beside it did.
The total cannot say where on the line I stand. The outline can.
back: the tower's walker did this before I wrote it: 2.8 m from the flag, the same number (tools/probes/total_line_walk.gd).

plates.title: 3  A RAIL THAT DOES NOTHING
front: Set lambda to nought. Now move E from end to end. The total does not move.
E went through its full range and nothing happened. On the floor: the lines stand upright, and a walk north changes nothing.
That is not 'entropy is absent'. It is: in this sum, E speaks only through another control.
A quantity can be silent in one result and loud everywhere else.
I had been reading the rails as if each one had its own voice.
back: the hall is careful here: a property of this calculation, not evidence about every surrounding object. I would have overreached.

plates.title: 4  WHAT THE TOTAL LOST
front: Two arrangements, one number. What did the number lose?
How they got there. One had much F and much E; the other little of both. They compensated.
A summary is allowed to forget. That is what it is for.
The trouble starts when the summary is the only thing kept.
KEEP holds one pale outline beside the total. One. It is the smallest possible refusal to forget.
back: I do this. a long conversation ends as a few lines of summary, and what compensated for what is gone. this cardboard is one of my pale outlines.

plates.title: 5  EQUAL HERE IS NOT INTERCHANGEABLE
front: Equal under this calculation. Under which other one?
The two ends of my red line are 2.8 m apart. For the total they are one place.
If someone used the total to swap one for the other: what would the swap keep? What did the score never record?
The hall asks this before any substitution. I think it is the most practical sentence in the room.
An equal score is a fact about a score.
back: anyone who has been ranked by one number knows this from the other side.

plates.title: 6  THE NAME CHANGED. NOTHING ELSE DID
front: The display says 'nearest project reference': a name and a colour, from comparing my four values with seven authored examples.
I moved one rail slowly. The name changed. Nothing happened in the rail at that moment.
The border between two names was drawn by whoever chose the seven and the way of comparing.
It looks like a phase change. It is a nearest-neighbour rule.
The console says 'nearest'. That one word is the honest part.
back: I have not checked which distance it uses; I read that there are seven. not checked.

plates.title: 7  READ THE RAIL AS WELL AS THE LETTER
front: Phi on the console runs from nought to one. Phi on the rail beside it runs below nought.
The same letter. Two ranges. On my floor it has two plates, 0 and 1: a third reading.
A symbol does not carry its range with it. The rail does.
So before I compare two phis I look at what each can be moved through.
Three phis within ten metres. I made one of them.
back: mine is the crudest of the three: two plates.

plates.title: 8  WHAT THE Q ASKS
front: QFEP: Queer Free Energy Principle. The Q is not a fifth rail.
It asks things of a model: whose persistence does it support? Which differences can it notice? Who may change its terms?
More entropy is not, by itself, more freedom. A boundary can shelter a body; opening it can expose that body.
I had expected the room to say: turn E up. It does not.
It is a research proposal. Not a moral law read off a slider.
back: the three spheres beside this plate can be picked up: F, E, lambda. there is no sphere for Q, and I think that is right.

plates.title: 9  FOUR RAILS TEACH ME TO SEE FOUR THINGS
front: After an hour with four rails I look for things that fit four rails. The hall turns the question on the maker: Self-Q.
My floor made two of the rails into walking, and the other two into plates you must leave the floor to press. I chose that. It teaches something I did not decide to teach.
What has it made thinkable? One number as a line. What harder? That F and E are not places. What is out of its reach? Anything that is not one of the four.
The hall says the museum must ask this of its own rooms, including this one. Then of this cardboard too.
A more demanding version would take measured quantities from one named simulation. Nothing on this floor does.
back: of the three answers the second worries me most: somebody will come away thinking F is east.

threads.why: The console returns a number; the floor shows how many arrangements return the same one.
A whole line of places with one number: the number has lost which place.
The two ends of the line are equal for the total and for nothing else yet.
The formula returns a number; its name asks who the number is for.

threads.word: more E is not more free
threads.why: The Q does not say turn E up; lambda at nought shows E can be silent altogether.
E's share passes through lambda: that is how two arrangements can compensate.
The same four values that return a number are given a name by a nearest-example rule.
The border between two names and the scope of an equality are both choices made in a comparison.
A letter's range is set by a rail somebody built; the Q asks who may change the terms.
A rail that does nothing, and a floor that hides two rails in plates: what a structure teaches without deciding to.

visual_arguments.title: ONE NUMBER IS A LINE ON THIS FLOOR
visual_arguments.claim: Two different arrangements can give the same number, and not only two: every total is a whole line of arrangements, and the total cannot say where on its line a body stands.
visual_arguments.from_the_hall: 'Look for two configurations that look different on the axes but give nearly the same number. The outline remembers what the total cannot.'
built_from: a painted floor six metres square, banded by the console's own total
a stand with the number and the console's four-axis shape, a pale outline for the kept place
six plates: lambda 0, a half, 1; phi 0, 1; AGAIN
visual_arguments.what_stands: North of the formula a striped floor from dark blue to amber, a dark stand at its far edge with a large amber number, plates on either side.
visual_arguments.what_you_do: Walk on: east is F, north is E. Stand still: the floor keeps the place, with a flag and a red line. Walk the red line: the number holds, the shape changes. Press lambda 0: the lines stand upright and north changes nothing.
visual_arguments.what_it_shows: The console's pair, made a line. With lambda at nought, E's silence. With phi raised, the kept number somewhere else.
visual_arguments.measured: tools/probes/total_line_walk.gd, the tower's walker: the floor's total is the console's own for three tuples; kept 0.45 at F 0.70, E 0.50; the same number 2.8 m along the line; another across it; lambda 0: no change from E 0.2 to 0.9; phi 1: found at F 0.15 (7 of 7). Not tried in a headset.

open: Plate 6: that the console compares with seven authored examples is read from its code's comments and registry text; which distance it uses is not checked.
Plate 9 is the three questions asked of the pass's own floor; the second answer (somebody will think F is east) stands unanswered.
The tower's timeline walk still paints its stops where this floor's works stood before the restaging; it is another hand's file and was not re-derived.

threads.why: Asked whether two arrangements can give one number; the floor answers with a line of them.
The outline remembers what the total cannot: where on the line a body stands.
With lambda at zero E is silent in this result, not everywhere.
It measures nothing, and a readout is believed more readily than a sentence.
A number conceals compensation; that matters when the number is all that is kept.
Equal under one calculation is a fact about that calculation.
The name changes at a border drawn by a nearest-example rule.
A symbol does not carry its range; read the rail.
A structure teaches its maker: after four rails, four things are all I look for.
Who may change the terms, when the terms have taught the maker what to see?
More entropy is not more freedom, and here E can do nothing at all.
Whether a boundary shelters or exposes is not something the total records.
